author: ojiudezue
title: v4.7.6 EVSE Solar-Aware Charging: hybrid A+B self_modulates flag + refined battery_ok + asymmetric SOC thresholds, upgraded to Tier 2-DB
summary: Live diagnostic post-v4.7.5 surfaced three compounding gate-logic bugs in EV/L1 pause behavior. (1) Drain-rule resume condition was `battery_ok or soc_recovered` where `battery_ok = not battery_discharging`, so URA's own pause caused solar to overflow into the battery, flipping `battery_ok` True, and URA immediately resumed EV — bouncing between paused and resumed mid-day. (2) Manual-override branch at energy_pool.py:553-561 treats Emporia's native solar-mode auto-restart identically to a user gesture and sets a 1-hour cooldown that suppresses both pause and resume — leaving the EVSE silently on. (3) Existing drain rule only acts on active discharge; doesn't pause when solar is fat enough to power EV plus trickle-charge battery, even though SOC may be far below user's preferred fill target. User wants URA to be the house-wide backstop: re-pause idempotently every tick, regardless of who turned it back on, with explicit user override via the Force-Charge button. The cycle folds in a UX rename (Excess Solar → EVSE Solar-Aware), 2 new Number entities for asymmetric SOC thresholds (95% turn-on, 80% pause-until), and 7 sensor attribute additions for observability. User explicitly upgraded review tier from 1 to 2-DB: 'since this code has been full of correctness issues.'

decisions.decision: Hybrid A+B semantics for the new per-EVSE `evse_self_modulates: bool` flag (default False / unchecked)
decisions.why: Option A alone (per-EVSE checkbox dictates behavior) leaves uncommunicative users stuck on whatever default we pick, and a wrong default broke them. Option B alone (observed-off + 30s grace state machine, auto-detect) is clever but has a race-condition tail for very fast smart re-enables that beat HA's state propagation. Hybrid: checkbox CHECKED → Option A behavior (idempotent re-pause, URA is authority, Force-Charge button is the user override path). Checkbox UNCHECKED (default OR unconfigured) → Option B (observed-off + grace state machine — only fires manual-override branch if URA observed `state.is_on=False` AND grace expired). Coverage matrix: smart EVSE checked → A clean. Smart EVSE unchecked → B auto-detects auto-resume as not-manual → still re-pauses. Dumb EVSE unchecked → B correctly treats user toggle as override after grace + observed-off. Dumb EVSE checked (misconfigured) → URA ignores override, re-pauses idempotently, user must Force-Charge. NO configuration leaves the user broken; default is safe; explicit opt-in is the optimization.
decisions.blast_radius: Per-EVSE config flow option + new sticky state (`_pause_dispatch_ts`, `_observed_off_since_pause`) in EVPool and SmartPlugPool. Adversarial test stubs needed for each of the 6 cells of the matrix. RestoreEntity vs reset semantics on the new state across HA restart — decided: reset (safer post-restart default than trusting stale state).

decisions.decision: Refined battery_ok: gate on `battery_soc <= reserve_soc + 2` to distinguish 'battery out of capacity' from 'transient equilibrium URA created'
decisions.why: Original `battery_ok` covered end-of-solar-day: battery hit reserve floor, Enphase management refused further discharge, battery_power_w clamps to ~0. At that point pausing EV doesn't help — battery's empty, grid is paying anyway. The bug case: mid-day at SOC=51 when URA's own pause causes solar to overflow into battery, `battery_ok` True for the wrong reason. The SOC discriminator separates them cleanly: at reserve_soc+2 the battery has truly nothing left to give; at SOC=51 it's transient. Preserves the original intent (resume when out of capacity) without false-resuming on equilibrium URA itself just created.
decisions.blast_radius: Single-line change at energy_pool.py:592 with conditional, plus dependency on `reserve_soc` which is already read by the battery coordinator. Test stubs: 'end-of-solar-day at reserve floor' (must resume) and 'transient equilibrium at SOC=51' (must NOT resume) — both required acceptance criteria.

decisions.decision: Asymmetric SOC thresholds: separate `fill_priority_soc` (80) and `excess_solar_soc` (95) Number entities — independent, live-tunable, big middle band
decisions.why: Single threshold forces symmetric semantics: 'turn on at X AND pause until X.' User wants generous middle band where neither rule fires and EV runs on its TOU schedule. Turn on at 95% (battery essentially full + sunny day → charge EV with surplus). Pause until 80% (battery low + sunny day → fill battery first). Between 80 and 95: neither rule active, EV follows TOU. Both Number entities mean live-tuning without reopening the config flow.
decisions.blast_radius: Two number entities + two CONFs + RestoreEntity round-trip via URA Mirror Pattern (entry 015). Acceptance: user can tune 80 → 75 live and see fill-priority pause trigger at SOC=74 within one tick.

decisions.decision: Rename `switch.ura_energy_coordinator_excess_solar_charging` → `switch.ura_energy_coordinator_evse_solar_aware_charging`; one switch gates both directions of the rule (turn-on AND pause)
decisions.why: Mental model is 'smart solar gating of EV charging' — same switch, two complementary directions. 'Excess Solar' only describes the surplus-driven turn-on; the new pause-until rule isn't an 'excess' condition. 'Solar-Aware' covers both. Keep unique_id stable so HACS history doesn't break. Provide entity_id alias for one release.
decisions.blast_radius: Friendly-name change + entity_id slug change + alias entry. Helper text updated. Force-Charge button helper-text cross-references the new self_modulates semantics. Reviewer C covers all three surfaces.

decisions.why: Today the user has to grep logs to figure out why an EVSE is or isn't paused. Worse, the manual-override cooldown is completely invisible — by the time you notice the silent-stuck-on state, the cooldown is already an hour in. 7 attrs surface: per-EVSE pause-reason-human one-liner, cooldown timer + WHY it engaged, fill_priority_target_soc echo, fill_priority_solar_ok bool, evse_config (self_modulates + source), pause_dispatch_state (dispatch_ts + observed_off + grace_expires). Together they make the state machine inspectable from a dashboard.
decisions.blast_radius: Sensor attribute additions only — no new entities. Reviewer C verifies render correctness on dashboards. Acceptance: every diagnostic question we had to debug live today must be answerable from the sensor attributes alone.

decisions.decision: Upgrade review tier from 1 to Tier 2-DB (3 parallel reviewers, different framings)
decisions.why: User-coined rationale: 'since this code has been full of correctness issues.' Doesn't match formal Tier 2-DB trigger criteria in CLAUDE.md (no database.py DAO changes, no migration, no payload-shape change). But the framing-discipline rationale applies: gate-logic in energy_pool.py has historically shipped correctness regressions (drain rule OR clause, manual-override false positive, cold-start race) that two similar reviewers would miss. Three reviewers with different framings: A (correctness + state-machine invariants — explicit state-machine table per (self_modulates, _paused_by_battery_drain∋evse_id, state.is_on, _observed_off_since_pause, grace) combination), B (async + lifecycle + restart resilience), C (new surfaces + admin UX + cross-rule precedence). Run in PARALLEL.
decisions.blast_radius: Three reviews fired in parallel after build. Likely surfaces more findings than a single review pass — accept that as the price of catching the residual correctness issues.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Drop the manual-override branch entirely (Option A everywhere)
alternatives_considered.why_rejected: Works perfectly for smart EVSEs but breaks dumb EVSEs where a user flipping the switch in HA SHOULD pause URA. User flagged: 'It will mean it works best with dumb EVSEs.' Hybrid A+B handles both classes with a safe default.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Pure Option B (observed-off + grace, no per-EVSE flag)
alternatives_considered.why_rejected: Has a race-condition tail: very fast smart re-enables that beat HA's state propagation could slip through grace without ever flipping observed_off. Hybrid lets the user explicitly opt in to the bulletproof Option A path for known-smart hardware.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Drop battery_ok entirely from resume condition (SOC-only resume)
alternatives_considered.why_rejected: Would strand EV off forever at night when battery is at reserve floor and grid is supplying. Refined `battery_out_of_capacity` (battery_ok AND soc<=reserve+2) preserves the original intent without the transient-equilibrium bug.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Single SOC threshold for both turn-on and pause (symmetric)
alternatives_considered.why_rejected: Forces user to choose between 'pause at 95 (won't pause until almost full)' or 'turn on at 80 (will run EV when battery only 80% full).' Asymmetric thresholds (turn on at 95, pause until 80) gives the dead-band where neither rule fires.
User explicit upgrade. Gate-logic history has correctness issues. Three framings can't share blind spots.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Two separate cycles — v4.7.6 hotfix (drain rule) then v4.7.7 (fill-priority + UX + rename)
alternatives_considered.why_rejected: User said no rush since solar's good today. Bundling avoids two deploys and two review cycles for what is essentially one coherent gate-logic rewrite. Acceptable risk because the safety-net (drain rule) and the new primary (fill-priority) are co-designed.

implications: Force-Charge button becomes the documented user-override path for smart EVSEs. Its UX gets cross-referenced from the renamed switch's helper text AND from the per-EVSE self_modulates checkbox's helper text. Triple-linking the override path is intentional — a silent-stuck-on state has been the dominant complaint.

Once `evse_self_modulates` ships, future EVSE integrations should default to False (unchecked) for safety — users can opt in to Option A after confirming their hardware's behavior. Document this as the convention in QUALITY_CONTEXT.md if it grows beyond two EVSEs.

Bug Class candidate (if cycle surfaces a new pattern): 'Resume Condition Too Broad — falses-resume on transient equilibrium our own pause created.' Battery drain's `battery_ok or soc_recovered` is the canonical example. Should be added to docs/QUALITY_CONTEXT.md as a new class if it recurs or if Reviewer A flags a similar pattern elsewhere.
Adversarial test pattern from this cycle (re-asserting state changes between dispatch and tick) is reusable for other URA backstop rules. Worth extracting as a test fixture once the build lands.
